study.title: Altered Hub Configurations within Default Mode Network following Acupuncture at ST36: A Multimodal Investigation Combining fMRI and MEG
study.study_design: parallel-group, between-subjects, single-block design, combining fMRI and MEG
study.blinding: participants instructed to keep eyes closed to prevent observing procedures; sham acupuncture used to reduce subjects' bias
study.population: 28 right-handed healthy college students (14 males, 14 females, aged 24.5±1.8 years) from a homogeneous group; all acupuncture naïve
study.inclusion_criteria: right-handed healthy college students, acupuncture naïve
study.exclusion_criteria: history of major medical illness, head trauma, neuropsychiatric disorders, or used any prescription medications within the last month

conditions.scan_context: resting state fMRI, eyes closed, no mental tasks

conditions.timepoint_exact: 9 min acupuncture procedure (1 min rest + 2 min needle manipulation + 6 min post-acupuncture rest)
conditions.scan_context: MEG recording during and after acupuncture

conditions.timepoint_exact: 6 min rest without acupuncture manipulation following 2 min needle manipulation

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: located four finger breadths below the lower margin of the patella and one finger breadth laterally from the anterior crest of the tibia, right leg
interventions.needle_type_exact: sterile disposable 38 gauge stainless steel acupuncture needle
interventions.needle_size_exact: 0.2 mm in diameter and 40 mm in length
interventions.penetration_exact: inserted perpendicularly into the skin surface
interventions.manipulation_exact: balanced 'tonifying and reducing' technique; twirling the needle clockwise and counter-clockwise equally; rotating the needle clockwise and counterclockwise for 1 min at a rate of 60 times per min
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: De-qi sensation intended; essential to the efficacy of acupuncture according to Traditional Chinese Medicine
interventions.needle_retention_exact: needle in for 2 min manipulation preceded by 1 min rest epoch and followed by 6 min rest
interventions.session_duration_exact: 9 min (1 min rest + 2 min needle manipulation + 6 min post-acupuncture rest)
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: experienced and licensed acupuncturist with 6 years of experience, trained to perform in the fMRI settings
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: remain relaxed without engaging in any mental tasks; eyes closed
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: ST36 is a commonly used acupoint for pain control in clinical practice

non_acupoint_locations_exact: non-meridian point, 2–3 cm apart from ST36, right leg
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: nearby nonacupoint on the right leg, 2–3 cm apart from ST36
interventions.penetration_exact: needling at non-meridian point; needle depth identical to verum
interventions.manipulation_exact: stimulation intensity and manipulation procedure all identical to those used in verum acupuncture; balanced 'tonifying and reducing' technique; rotating the needle clockwise and counterclockwise for 1 min at a rate of 60 times per min
interventions.needle_retention_exact: same as verum: 2 min manipulation preceded by 1 min rest epoch and followed by 6 min rest
interventions.session_duration_exact: 9 min (1 min rest + 2 min needle manipulation + 6 min post-acupuncture rest)
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: same experienced and licensed acupuncturist with 6 years of experience
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: remain relaxed without engaging in any mental tasks; eyes closed
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: sham acupuncture used as a control to reveal acupoint-specific response

sham_details.sham_subtype_exact: non-meridian point needling (NAP), 2–3 cm apart from ST36
sham_details.sham_location_exact: nearby nonacupoint on the right leg, 2–3 cm apart from ST36
sham_details.sham_manipulation_exact: identical to verum: rotating the needle clockwise and counterclockwise for 1 min at a rate of 60 times per min

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: 3.0 T MRI system (Allegra; Siemens, Erlangen, Germany); MEG: CTF Systems Inc., Port Coquitlam, BC, Canada, whole head MEG system consisting of 151 hardware first-order magnetic gradiometers
neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: T2*-weighted single-shot, gradient-recalled echo planar imaging sequence (fMRI); 3D MRI sequences for structural (TR=2700 ms, TE=2.19 ms, matrix=384×512, FOV=256 mm×256 mm, flip angel=7°, thickness=1 mm)
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: functional: FOV=240 mm×240 mm, matrix=64×64, thickness=5 mm; structural: voxel size of 1 mm3; resampled at 2 mm×2 mm×2 mm
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: fMRI: 6 minutes resting state; MEG: 15 minutes total (6 min resting state + 9 min acupuncture procedure)
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: SPM5 (http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm/); GIFT (Group ICA of fMRI Toolbox); BESA (Brain Electrical Source Analysis, MEGIS Software GmbH, Germany)
neuroimaging_methods.normalization_template_exact: standard Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) template provided by SPM5; MNI 152 standard space
neuroimaging_methods.coordinate_space_reported_exact: Talairach coordinates (Table 1 regional sources); MNI 152 (Fig. 2 fMRI spatial DMN components)
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: Gaussian kernel with a full width at half maximum of 6 mm (FWHM=6 mm)
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: None of subjects had head movements exceeding 1 mm on any axis or head rotation greater than one degree; head displacements within a recording session below 5 mm (MEG)
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: fMRI: finite-impulse response band-pass filter (0.01~0.08 Hz); MEG: band-pass of 0.5–48 Hz, down-sampled at 300 Hz; subsequently band-passed into: delta (0.5–4 Hz), theta (4–8 Hz), alpha (8–13 Hz), beta (13–30 Hz), gamma band (30–48 Hz)

extraction_notes.note: Adverse events are not reported anywhere in the paper. No statement is made that adverse events did or did not occur.

Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success measures (beyond ensuring eyes closed and acupuncture-naïve participants) are not reported. No formal expectancy or credibility instrument was administered.

Randomization of participants to arms is not explicitly described; the paper states '28 participants were evenly divided into two groups, one for ST36 and the other for NAP, being matched by age and gender' but does not specify random allocation.

Exact numeric values for MASS sensation frequency percentages (Fig. 3A) and intensity scores (Fig. 3B) are shown only in bar charts and are not readable from the PDF text. Only the aching sensation was explicitly highlighted in text as greater for ST36.

The coordinate space of Table 1 is labeled 'Talairach coordinates' but the fMRI group ICA images (Fig. 2) are described as overlaid on MNI 152 space. The MEG source seeding used Talairach coordinates from Table 1. These are two different spaces used for different purposes.
Two MEG channels (out of 151) were not available due to technical problems during recording for all participants; effectively 149 channels were used for all participants.

The paper uses Talairach coordinates in Table 1 for MEG source seeding but does not explicitly state whether these were directly from Talairach space or converted from MNI. The fMRI data was normalized to MNI template.

The resting-state MEG data used for functional connectivity analysis covers 360 seconds (6 min), but it is unclear whether hub configurations for 'REST' refer to the pre-acupuncture MEG rest and whether the same 28 participants contributed to REST vs the 14 per arm for NAP and ST36 post-conditions.
Clinical behavioral outcomes (e.g., pain ratings, clinical efficacy) were not assessed; this was a healthy volunteer neuroimaging study with no clinical endpoint.
The paper does not specify sham needle type or diameter. The NAP uses what appears to be a real penetrating needle at a non-meridian location, not a non-penetrating sham device.

The n_analyzed for REST hub configuration analysis is reported as 28 (all subjects combined) based on the total sample, but since groups were between-subjects, the REST data collected during MEG for NAP group (n=14) and ST36 group (n=14) may have been analyzed separately or pooled. The paper refers to 'REST' hub configurations without specifying per-group breakdown.

Table 3 (delta), Table 4 (theta), Table 5 (alpha), Table 6 (beta), Table 7 (gamma) include P-values for paired t-test comparisons between ST36 and NAP (labeled 'P-value' in ST36 column). However, the REST column P-value refers to one-sample t-test significance of the connectivity itself, not a comparison. This distinction was preserved in the extraction.

For functional connectivity tables (Tables 3-7), P-values in the NAP column represent paired t-test comparing NAP post vs REST, and P-values in the ST36 column represent paired t-test comparing ST36 post vs REST (or emergence/suspension). The header labels 'P-value' under NAP and ST36 represent different comparisons. Extracted accordingly.

The hub configuration summary (Table 2) lists hubs per condition and band. Individual hub entries were extracted from both Table 2 and corroborated by the text descriptions in results. Where Table 2 and text were consistent, both were used.
